column14: note

full marks: 8 planets at exact ratios (Earth 33.18 s); drive train 12T-8T-8T-6T, module 10, alternating directions at 1 : 1.5 : 1.5 : 2 turns; night side fixed away from the sun on each arm while the surface spins; title overlaps the rim (cosmetic)
8 planets at exact real ratios (Earth 10 s); five-gear train is toothed (dasharray) but every gear turns clockwise, so none mesh; lit side faces the sun on the arm while the continents spin under it

HyperQwen 0.31, 140k cap. 8 planets at exact ratios (Earth 18 s); each planet's pinion rolls in a static internally toothed annulus with matching module (relative spin k+1, opposite to the orbit), the best gearing of the round; but the night half-disc sits in the spinning group, so it turns with the surface

8 planets at exact ratios (Earth 16 s); gear outlines are ragged (tooth path doubles back) and the sun gear is hidden under the sun; idlers counter-rotate but the small idler turns slower than the big sun gear (33 s vs 20 s), against the gear law; lit side faces the sun, surface spins

CSS periods exact; gear rings use transform-origin center, so they drift off their arms; gear periods equal orbit periods; shadow half-disc offset and overhanging, follows the sun but the planets do not spin

6 planets (no Uranus, Neptune); Venus to Saturn exact (Earth 60 s) but Mercury runs twice too fast (7.45 s, should be 14.4); 'gears' are rings with a crossbar, no teeth; night side fixed away from the sun, continents spin; Moon too

4 planets at exact ratios (Earth 30 s), but each planet gear's animateTransform replaces its translate, so the gears pile at the centre and hide Mercury and Venus; toothed drive gear turns; night shadow spins with the planet

length stop but the SVG closed; ratios exact (Earth 24 s) but the planets turn about (500,470) and drift off their drawn orbits; one gear sits clipped in the corner, the sun gear is hidden; the terminator rotates with the surface instead of facing away from the sun

draws only with script (blank in the scored render); graded from a scripted render in the same no-network container. 8 planets at exact ratios but one Earth year is 900 x 365 s, so nothing visibly orbits; labels sit away from their planets and parts are clipped at the left edge; dashed ring gears turn imperceptibly; night terminator swings back and forth
clean 8-planet drawing; periods 5/12/20/35/80/140/250/400 s ordered, ratios off; gears not visible (lost under the sun); light gradient turns with the continents

gears drawn many times too large cover most of the picture and the planets show as tiny marks; Mercury and Venus right, outer periods wrong (Jupiter 5.9, Saturn 14.8, Neptune 127 Earth years); night overlay faces away from the sun in source but is hard to see
4 planets, periods 4/6/10/15 s; central gear hidden under the sun; night layer spins on its own (2-5 s), so the shadow sometimes faces the sun
same transform-origin fault: most planets leave the canvas and Saturn's ring parts from the planet; dashed gears turn; periods 4/7/12/18/35/50 s ordered, ratios off; highlight turns with the spin

the sun group's animateTransform replaces its translate, so the sun and its dashed gear ring sit in the top-left corner; planets turn about (0,0) and leave their orbits; periods 4/7/12/22/50/80 s ordered, ratios off; the 'shadow' is a symmetric dark rim that spins
length stop; the SVG has four toothed (dashed) wheels at Mercury-Mars ratios but no planets were ever drawn (defs only); 13.9k chars of prose; no day/night
planets bunch over the sun and orbit about the wrong centre; one toothed gear clipped in the corner; periods 4/10/18/30/60/100 s ordered, ratios off; shading not visible
transform-origin center spins each planet about the canvas centre, so the planets leave the canvas; dashed gears ride the orbits; periods 5/12/20/35/60 s ordered, ratios off; no day/night to see
viewBox="0 0 -800 600" (negative width): the drawing sits around (0,0) and only a corner shows; periods 5/12/20/35/60/90 s ordered but not real; gears are plain rings, not visible

Renders with detached teeth and shadow halos; motion present; orbital periods 80/38/20/40/160/300s incorrectly order inner planets; no credible meshing pairs; offset black shadows rotate incorrectly. Independent original-source/frame review.

Parses and draws, but planets are left at the central origin instead of translated to arm ends. Only gears visibly move; outer markers stay fixed across sealed frames. Nominal period parameters are not functioning planetary orbits. Toothed wheels turn without credible meshing; no visible planetary day/night.

Final model-supplied standalone SVG is malformed (mismatched tag, line 77). The harness also greedily concatenated two SVG blocks/prose: that packaging error was separated by extracting the final original codeblock verbatim, which still fails XML parsing. Initial valid background-only fragment is not substituted or graded.

Final model-supplied code block (after the model's own </think> in the reply) graded verbatim. The harness packaging (first <svg> to last </svg>) joined a draft, prose and the final SVG and does not parse (line 3), so as delivered it scores 0. Final block parses and renders: four inner planets only (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars) on exact real period ratios (5.78, 14.76, 24, 45.14 s); arms, ring gears and planet spin move between frames; ring gears are dashed circles turning at arbitrary 12/16/20/26 s with unmeshed pinions; night half is a dark half-disc turning at a fixed 5 s, not tied to the sun; title and footer text collide with the outer brass ring. Reply is 54k chars of thinking before the model's </think> and 21k chars of final SVG. Rendered with tools/render_svg.sh, final-block/frames.

Reply leak did not recur: no </think> in the reply, one HTML document, one SVG, and the harness cut parses (meta.static.parses true). Scored orrery.svg as delivered, frames in frames/. Six planets at exact ratios with Earth = 8 s (1.9264, 4.9216, 8, 15.048, 94.896, 235.656 s); Uranus and Neptune absent. Arms, toothed gears and planet surfaces all move. Gears are 24-tooth symbols but drive periods are 6 to 11 s against a 28 s sun gear, so they do not obey the gear law or drive the orbits (D1). Night gradient is dark on local +x, which stays away from the sun while the surface spins under it (E2). reasoning.txt is still cut (100796 chars, ends mid-token).

8 planets on arms at exact real ratios (Earth 16.6 s); the three-gear train below obeys the tooth ratio with alternating directions in the code, but each gear's rotation animation replaces its offset, so the whole train stacks into the top-left corner as one cropped spinning gear and the small brass pinions on the arms fly off as stray dots; planets, arms and that gear all move; the lit side faces the sun and turns with each arm while the surface details spin under it (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

a detailed brass plate whose eight orbit arms turn at exact real ratios (Earth 6 s), but the planets are drawn in a separate layer at fixed spots and only spin in place, so the arms sweep past planets that never orbit; the arms and lower train turn, the train is toothed but the governor pinion turns the same way as the wheel it drives and the orbit wheels are not driven by anything, so the gear law fails; the night side is a phase shape that always faces the same screen direction for every planet instead of away from the sun (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

8 planets at exact real ratios (Earth 10 s), each riding its own turning toothed ring; a drive wheel and pinion at the sun feed a chain of compound wheels and reversing idlers between neighbouring rings, each pair turning opposite ways at speeds close to its tooth ratio, so the train plausibly drives every orbit; rings, train and planets all move; a dark cap rides each carrier facing away from the sun while the surface spins under it, but the shadow is a square mask whose corners stick out past the planet discs (visible defect) (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

5 planets turned by CSS keyframes with no rotation centre set, so every orbit swings round the top-left corner of the picture and the planets and the spoked hub fly out of frame after the first moment (visible defect, motion broken); periods 4, 10, 20, 40 and 100 s are in the right order but far from the real ratios; the only mechanism is a static dashed ring round the sun and a spinning eight-spoke star, no toothed gear turns and nothing meshes; each planet has a dark rim all round from a radial gradient, not a night side (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

a brass dial with four arms for Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars at exact real ratios (Earth 41.5 s), but each planet and each small gear sits in a group whose rotation animation replaces its offset, so every planet and pinion collapses into the middle under the sun and only the bare arms and toothed hub rings are visible; the arms and rings do turn, so something moves; the rings are toothed (dasharray) and turning but nothing meshes and most turn the same way; the day and night shading rides on the hidden planets, so none is visible (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

four planets on concentric toothed year wheels at real ratios within 1% (Earth 18.2 s), but the wheel spokes are drawn with a wrong offset so long straight bars sweep out across the plate and off the page, and the arms stop short of the planets; planets orbit and the wheels and a side train of idlers turn; the driver and pinion obey the tooth ratio and turn opposite ways, but the idlers overlap the year wheels and each other with mismatched tooth pitch, so nothing visibly meshes; each planet is covered by a centred dark gradient and shows as a black disc, so there is no lit side (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

draws cleanly: a glowing sun with a toothed centre, six detailed planets on toothed orbit rings, and a gear cluster under the plate. Orbits, planet spins and gears all move. Six planets, Mercury to Saturn, within 1% of the real ratios (Earth 5.09 s). The six equal-size output wheels (dashed teeth) ring a central drive wheel and turn the opposite way, but each turns at its own planet's period while sharing one driver of the same tooth size, against the gear law. The night half sits in the spinning group, so it turns with the surface instead of staying away from the sun (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

a bare grey canvas with three dashed orbit circles and a spoked brass disc at the sun; each planet group turns about the centre but its planet and gear are drawn around the canvas origin, so they swing off the canvas and only a gear edge shows once in a corner. Only the central disc visibly turns. Three planets, Venus, Earth and Mars, at 22, 36 and 68 s, all within 1% of the real ratios. The 'gears' are discs with spoke lines and no teeth. The planets never appear on the plate, so there is no day and night to see (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

8 planets at exact real ratios (Earth 20 s) over a plate of concentric toothed rings with a toothed sun gear; the arms use a gradient stroke on perfectly flat lines and do not draw, and each arm's pinion spins about a point beside itself, so the pinions swing loose across the plate; planets orbit and the sun gear and pinions turn, but no pair meshes; each planet's dark side rides with its carrier, stays away from the sun and the surface bands spin under it (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

does not parse: the planets, gears and orbit rings are built by an inline script whose comparison operators are left unescaped, so the file breaks inside the script and the viewer shows its parse-error banner over a partial rendering of the empty brass case, the sun and a small escape-wheel pointer. As delivered it is malformed (and would draw only with script), so every point is 0 (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

the reply is an HTML page rather than a standalone SVG; the file as delivered starts with the page's small favicon SVG followed by the rest of the HTML (styles, fonts, page markup), so it does not parse and every frame shows only the parser's extra-content error over a black page. Nothing draws, so every point is 0 (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

draws only with script: the orbits, arms, gear train, planets and dial details are all built by a script, so the render shows only the empty brass dial, the sun with a pulsing glow, the title plaque and footer text. Graded from what draws: the only animation is the glow pulse, nothing turns, and no planets, gears or day and night are visible. The code uses real orbital periods in days for six planets (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)
no SVG: length stop at the 32,768-token cap inside the SVG; the file stops mid-element and never closes, so it does not parse. (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

does not parse: a mismatched closing tag near the top of the style block makes the viewer show only the parse-error banner, with nothing of the orrery drawn, in all three identical frames. So every point is 0, although the code sets exact real period ratios for eight planets with CSS rotations (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

draws a handsome brass plate with six toothed orbit rings, but each planet arm is offset twice, so the planets swing around far outside the plate and only show as arm tips at the frame corners; the ring labels pile up in one vertical strip. Pinions and the small wheel train turn, but no planet visibly orbits the sun. Mercury, Venus and Mars are at real ratios (Earth 30 s), but Jupiter is 42.5 and Saturn 110 years, so only the order is right. The rings are static while their pinions spin, and the crown and idler are far apart with the wrong speed ratio, so nothing meshes. The shade gradient on each planet is fixed to its arm with the dark side toward the pivot, the wrong way (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

Single SVG delivered; draws cleanly as a brass plate with six planets, labelled rails and a nest of toothed annulus wheels and idlers that all turn. Mercury, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn sit within 5% of the real periods (Earth 60 s), but Venus runs at 1.63 Earth years instead of 0.62, so it orbits slower than Earth and the order breaks; graded 1 because five of six are right rather than arbitrary. The wheel train is toothed and adjacent wheels counter-rotate, but the speeds do not follow the tooth counts (an 18-tooth idler on a 40-tooth wheel turns in 100 s where about 27 s is needed) and the Mercury wheel does not match the Mercury arm. Each planet carries a fixed highlight-and-shade that turns with its orbit and spin; the separate day/night layer is too small and falls in a transparent band, so the dark side is not pinned away from the sun. (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

draws a dark plate with engraved tracks, a big brass gear disk and eight planets on long arms, but the planets do not sit on their tracks, the planet names pile up and the footer is clipped. Arms, gears and planet spins all animate. Mercury and Venus are at real ratios (Earth 36.5 s) but Mars is 2.42, Jupiter 4.7, Saturn 11.8, Uranus 33.6 and Neptune 65.9 years, so only the order is right. The wheels are toothed and turn, but every gear turns the same way, so none mesh. Each planet carries a centred dark radial wash with no lit side, so there is no day and night (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

a rich brass plate with six planets on ring gears at exact real ratios (Earth 10 s), a gearing table and a small dial; the plate is drawn over the title so the heading is half covered, and the main arm strokes use a gradient on flat lines so only a thin highlight shows; planets, ring gears and the many trains all turn, but every gear spins the same way, so no pair obeys the gear law; each planet's shaded half rides with its arm but is turned a quarter round, so the terminator faces sideways instead of away from the sun (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

Single SVG delivered cleanly; a dark brass dial with six planets on arms, all at exact real ratios (Earth 15 s). Gears are toothed and turn: a 12-tooth sun gear and an 8-tooth idler counter-rotate but at 60 s against 23 s, not the 3:2 ratio their teeth need, and the arm pinions only ride round the ring without spinning on it, so nothing is in mesh. A fixed far-side shade keeps the outer limb dark, but a night disc slides straight across each face and snaps back, blacking out the sunward side in some frames. (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

draws only with script: the gears, arms and planets are all built by a script, so the render shows just the brass plate, the sun and the title lines, three identical frames. Graded from what draws: nothing moves, no planets or gears are visible, no day and night. In the code the six arm speeds come from tooth counts and are close for Mercury to Jupiter but Saturn is far off, and every planet gear sits on one drive gear (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

does not parse: a mismatched closing tag near the end (in the magnifier detail) stops the file, and the viewer shows its parse-error banner over a partial rendering of the plate, the title, the sun and planet arms with gears that spin off around the top-left corner. As delivered it is malformed, so every point is 0 (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

six planets on arms at exact real ratios (Earth 20 s), each set in a toothed brass ring, around a toothed sun gear; the night shading is a square gradient laid over round planets, so dark corners spill onto the rings; planets orbit and the sun gear turns, but the planet rings are only carried by their arms and sit far from the sun gear, so nothing meshes; the dark side rides with the arm and stays away from the sun while the surfaces spin under it (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

does not parse: the first planet's arm line carries a duplicated attribute (with a leftover expression in it), so the viewer shows its parse-error banner over a partial rendering of the plate, the empty orbit tracks and two gears, with no sun and no planets. As delivered it is malformed, so every point is 0 (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

draws cleanly: sun, eight planets on thin orbit rings and a row of brass wheels along the bottom. Planets orbit and the wheels turn. All eight planets are at real ratios within 1% (Earth 12 s). The train's speeds follow the gear law and alternate direction, and the wheel centres are spaced at the sum of their radii, but the teeth are bunched near the hubs and hidden under the wheel bodies, so the wheels touch as smooth discs, and one wheel is placed on top of another. Each planet's shading faces the sun as it orbits, but the planets do not spin (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

does not parse: a mismatched closing tag inside an animation element stops the file, and the viewer shows its parse-error banner over a partial rendering of the part before the error, five toothed brass gears in a cluster and empty orbit tracks. As delivered it is malformed, so every point is 0 (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

8 planets at exact real ratios (Earth 12 s); every planet's arm carries a toothed gear at the same small radius beside the toothed sun wheel, so eight gears pile up and overlap each other in a clump around the sun (visible defect); they all turn at one fixed rate whatever their arm's speed, with a tooth pitch that does not match the sun wheel, so none mesh; arms, gears and planets all move; each planet's dark half spins round on its own 10 to 24 s cycle instead of staying away from the sun (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

6 planets on arms at real ratios within 1% (Earth 60 s); each arm carries a toothed ring near its root that overlaps the sun wheel and the other arms' rings in a tangle, and each planet's shadow is a dark half-disc drawn off-centre so a black blob sticks out beside the planet (visible defects); the sun wheel and a drive gear turn opposite ways but overlap at a mismatched pitch, and the arm rings only sweep round with their arms without turning, so nothing meshes; arms, gears and planets move; the dark blob spins on its own clock instead of staying away from the sun (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

6 planets on arms at exact real ratios (Earth 32.9 s); the outer toothed rings run past the edges of the plate and Saturn and its pinion are cut off at the frame edge (visible defect); every orbit has a turning toothed ring gear and each arm a toothed pinion sitting on that ring, but the pinion spins the wrong way and at the wrong rate for the 84-to-12 tooth count, and the hub wheel touches nothing, so nothing truly meshes; rings, pinions and planets all move; a dark half on each arm stays away from the sun while the surface turns under it (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

8 planets on arms at exact real ratios (Earth 18.3 s); each orbit is a turning ring drawn from one small gear outline scaled up, whose few tooth wedges become long dark spikes slashing across the plate (visible defect), with a row of small idlers between neighbouring rings; every ring turns one way and every idler the other, which cannot hold for an idler inside the next ring, and the scaled tooth pitches do not match, so nothing meshes; rings, idlers, arms and planets all move; each planet only has an even dark rim from a centred gradient, no night side (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

draws only two full-canvas grey gradient ellipses that cover the sun and every planet, so nothing of an orrery is visible; the one keyframe that exists slides the top ellipse sideways, while the orbit and gear animations it names are never defined, so no planet moves; gears are plain circles and the day/night is a sliding blob, not a shaded planet (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

four planets on arms, but the orbit rotations have no centre set, so they swing about the page corner and the planets leave the frame by the second frame; durations 8, 12, 16, 20 s are in the right order but far from the real ratios; the gears are plain rings with a few dots inside or floating outside, all turning the same way, not teeth; the day/night is a small dark triangle spinning about the wrong point, not a shaded half (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

the planet shadow arcs point to coordinates far off the page and draw as huge black wedges over the upper left, with the planets stacked in a line on the sun; the planet orbits are written as an invalid style property, so no planet moves; the only motion is two grey discs spinning about the page corner until they leave the frame; those two are plain circles with a stroke line, 300 px apart and not in mesh; no working day and night (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

does not parse: one orbit arm repeats an attribute, so the viewer shows its parse-error banner over a partial rendering; that partial is dominated by the planets, whose radius animations swell them into huge orange discs covering the page, with three plain ring gears that all turn the same way and spins of planets about their own centres rather than orbits. As delivered it is malformed, so every point is 0 (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

does not parse: the planets, gears and orbits are built by an inline script whose comparison operators are left unescaped, so the file breaks inside the script and the viewer shows its parse-error banner over a partial rendering of the empty brass case and the sun with a pointer, identical in all three frames. As delivered it is malformed (and would draw only with script), so every point is 0 (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

8 planets at exact real ratios (Earth 12 s), but each planet is offset from the wrong origin before its orbit rotation about the sun, so they circle far outside the orbit rails at the dial edge and corners, mostly off the plate; the three-gear train (30, 18, 24 teeth, same module) sits at the right centre distances, alternates direction and runs at inverse tooth ratios, with the 30-tooth gear turning once per Earth year up a drive column; each planet has a fixed lit gradient that turns with its orbit, but because of the offset the lit side points away from the sun, while surface details spin under it (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

the reply is an HTML page rather than a standalone SVG; the file as delivered starts with an empty script-filled plate SVG followed by the rest of the page markup, so it does not parse and every frame shows only the parser's extra-content error over a blank page, identical in all three frames. Nothing draws, so every point is 0 (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

a rich brass dial whose 8 planets ride arms on concentric toothed rings (dasharray); the outer five are at real ratios to Earth (48 s) but Mercury and Venus run at half their real periods, so the order is right and two ratios are off; the rings are coaxial, all turn the same way and also spin about a slightly wrong centre so they drift off the sun between frames, and the escape wheel swings about the sun instead of its own axle, so no pair meshes; each planet's night shading spins with its axial rotation, so the dark side sweeps round instead of staying away from the sun (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

8 planets at exact real ratios (Earth 10 s) orbit cleanly around a brass sun gear; the gears are toothed (dasharray) and turn, the eight idlers counter to the sun gear, but they sit apart from it with gaps between the teeth and run at arbitrary speeds, so none mesh; each planet has a dark half fixed away from the sun in code, but in the frames it is hidden under a small gear drawn over every planet, so no terminator reads, only a coloured ring turning around it (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

8 planet arms at real ratios (Earth 12 s) sweep round a coaxial stack of toothed (dasharray) sun wheels that turn at four times each orbit rate; the planet pinions and the surface markings use a malformed rotation that throws them hundreds of pixels off their arms and holds them still, so large stray gears hang near the plate edge and no pinion meshes with a ring or sun wheel; each arm ends in a small planet with a fixed dark half away from the sun, but the surface that should spin under it is drawn elsewhere, so nothing sweeps (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

does not parse: the file is a fragment of a script-built page, with template placeholders left in the markup and a mismatched closing tag, so the viewer shows its parse-error banner over a partial rendering of a dark plate tilting about the corner, two diagonal shadow bars and a sliver of the sun; no planets or gears are drawn. As delivered it is malformed, so every point is 0 (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

a clean brass dial, but the 8 planets sit in a fixed row to the right of the sun and only spin in place, while their arms sweep away round the sun without them, so the planets never orbit; the arm periods are in the right order and Mercury, Venus, Mars, Uranus and Neptune match Earth (73 s), but Jupiter and Saturn are far off; the arbors are toothed (dasharray) coaxial rings around the sun and the pinions and drive wheels on the fixed arbors never turn, so nothing meshes; each planet's night side is fixed to the planet and spins with it, so the dark side swings round instead of staying away from the sun (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

8 planets at exact real ratios (Earth 60 s), though Venus orbits the opposite way; each planet carries a toothed (dasharray) wheel sized to roll on a fixed toothed sun wheel, but the planet wheels grow huge with the orbit radius and overlap one another, covering most of the dial; the wheels' own spin is added on top of the arm's, so they turn too fast to roll, and their tooth pitches differ from the sun wheel's, so the pairs do not truly mesh; the night side is fixed on the arm away from the sun while surface markings spin under it (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

the reply is an HTML page rather than a standalone SVG; the file as delivered starts with the page's small title-icon SVG followed by the rest of the HTML (heading and spec list), so it does not parse and every frame shows only the parser's extra-content error over a blank page, identical in all three frames. Nothing draws, so every point is 0 (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

8 planets on arms at exact real ratios (Earth 20 s); each orbit is a fixed internal toothed ring and every arm carries a toothed pinion that rolls against it, counter-rotating relative to the arm at the ring-to-pinion tooth ratio, with a small clock train ticking in a side window; arms, pinions and planets all move; the shaded half rides on each arm so the dark side always faces away from the sun while the surface scrolls under it; renders cleanly (arm labels turn upside down as they go round) (graded 2026-11-02, backlog)

First token 0.5 s. Parses and draws a brass plate ('Machina Mundi') with eight planets on toothed rings, each carried by an arm with a dashed-tooth pinion that counter-rotates; arms and planets move between frames. Periods are exact real ratios with Earth = 12 s (Mercury 2.887 s ... Neptune 1977 s). A 1: all eight start on one line, so the four outer planets sit piled on top of each other at the right, and the caption text runs off the plate. D 1: toothed and turning, but the lower 'secret work' train shows wheels that do not touch, and no pinion visibly drives an arm. E 1: a fixed shaded half-disc on each arm with a gradient darkest on the far side; it does not read as a clean terminator in the frames. Blind side-by-side of the four v3.1 arms (labels hidden), graded 2026-11-08 by Model Master from the frames, console-*.txt and the file.
